{"id": "9cb27872-4ec5-427e-b2f3-344b46c1bf7d", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Here's a CloudFormation template for an S3 bucket with sensible security defaults (encryption, versioning, and public access blocked):

```yaml
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: '2010-09-09'
Description: S3 bucket with encryption, versioning, and public access blocked

Parameters:
  BucketNameParam:
    Type: String
    Description: Globally unique name for the S3 bucket
    Default: my-app-bucket

Resources:
  MyS3Bucket:
    Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
    Properties:
      BucketName: !Ref BucketNameParam
      VersioningConfiguration:
        Status: Enabled
      BucketEncryption:
        ServerSideEncryptionConfiguration:
          - ServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
              SSEAlgorithm: AES256
      PublicAccessBlockConfiguration:
        BlockPublicAcls: true
        BlockPublicPolicy: true
        IgnorePublicAcls: true
        RestrictPublicBuckets: true
      Tags:
        - Key: Name
          Value: !Ref BucketNameParam

Outputs:
  BucketName:
    Description: Name of the created S3 bucket
    Value: !Ref MyS3Bucket
  BucketArn:
    Description: ARN of the created S3 bucket
    Value: !GetAtt MyS3Bucket.Arn
```

A few notes:
- `BucketName` is parameterized — S3 bucket names must be globally unique, so you'll want to change the default or pass your own value at deploy time.
- Encryption (AES256/SSE-S3) and versioning are on by default; swap to `aws:kms` with a `KMSMasterKeyID` if you need customer-managed keys.
- Public access is fully blocked, which is the recommended baseline unless you specifically need a public bucket (e.g., static website hosting).
